Commentary.Commentary: That is it from this match! Zimbabwe take 1-0 lead in this 3-match series. The 2nd match will be played on Friday, September 10 at 10.30 am local (9.30 am GMT). Do join us for that. Till then, adios and take care!

Craig Ervine, the Zimbabwe skipper says, that the first 10-15 overs were difficult for batting and applauds Brendan Taylor for batting the way that he did and the foundation was nicely laid. He adds that he was happy with the total on the board and 266 was always going to be tough to chase. Also adds that he would have liked to pick up some early wickets but the bowlers stuck to their plan and the spinners bowled tightly as well, which helped them.

Sikandar Raza is THE MAN OF THE MATCH, he says that the foundation was set early on and especially by Brendan Taylor and he was delighted to see senior guys setting it up and the wicket got better when he came on to bat. He adds that he just wanted to go out their with a positive intent and run hard between the wickets and luckily for him, that's what he managed to do.
... THE PRESENTATION ...

Earlier in the day, it was the skipper of Zimbabwe, Craig Ervine who was the commander in their bating. With some quick cameos, earlier from Taylor and in the fag end of the innings from Raza powered Zimbabwe to 266 for 7.  Stay tuned for the Presentation.

Zimbabwe were disciplined with their lines and lengths. They started off poorly but once they got the first breakthrough, the doors for wicket were wide opened. Porterfield and Tector did stitch a partnership but Luke Jongwe started his second spell brilliantly as he removed the former man. The game was poised till the 40th over but then came Blessing Muzarabani, he was outstanding as he removed the dangerous Harry Tector and after that, it was just finishing the things. Blessing Muzarabani was the figurehead of the bowlers as he scalped 4 wickets. Other bowlers helped him and finished the job comfortably.

It looked like an easy win at one point but the wickets of William Porterfield and Harry Tector changed the scenario. Ireland were off to a great start, both the openers crawled to a 50-run partnership before Paul Stirling gave away his wicket. The runs were not flowing at the required rate but the Irish were staying in the hunt. Once Harry Tector walked out, the momentum changed, and with him and William Porterfield, both managed to stitch a partnership of 71. Once Porterfield fell, the hopes for the win were with Tector but he too fell just after making his 50 and with him, the hopes of a win perished. The win was almost there for Ireland if someone had kept the composure and stayed out in the middle till the end but they were second best and will be a little bit disappointed with their batting performance.
An excellent bowling display from Zimbabwe. They go on to lead this 3-match series by going 1-0 up as they were superior throughout the match.

OUT! TAKEN! That's it, Zimbabwe have done it. Blessing Muzarabani pitches this one up and Little looks to hit it over the long off fence. Little miscues it and the ball goes high and over mid off. Craig Ervine tracks back and takes a fine catch. Blessing Muzarabani ends with a four-fer. ZIMBABWE WIN BY 38 RUNS!

DRINKS BREAK - Ireland took the slow and steady approach to the chase and were successful up to an extent. Paul Stirling settled in and started playing his shots, but just when it all looked good, Stirling got out and Ireland have to re-build. Zimbabwe were brilliant in the first Powerplay and Ngarava, along with Muzarabani bowled really well. They, however, did not get any wickets and couldn't apply much pressure. Wellington Masakadza finally provided the breakthrough and the chase is nicely poised at the moment.

OUT! LBW! Wellington Masakadza gets the dangerous Paul Stirling! A full ball, angling on middle. Stirling gets inside the line of the ball and looks to sweep but seems to miss and gets hit on the pads. The ball lobs in front of Stirling and the keeper catches it. They appeal and up goes the finger. Stirling straightaway reviews the decision. UltraEdge confirms no bat. Ball Tracker shows three reds and Ireland lose their review.

Paul Stirling has reviewed the umpire's decision. There will be a check for both LBW and the catch. UltraEdge shows that there's no bat or glove on it. Ball-Tracker shows three reds and Paul Stirling has to make the long walk to the pavilion. Ireland lose the review as well.

Nicely tossed up, around off. Stirling pushes it to sweeper cover and collects a run.
Wellington Masakadza is into the attack.
FOUR LEG BYES! Blessing Muzarabani ruins his figures a bit on the final ball. Spills it down the leg side. William Porterfield tickles it fine off the pads and the ball races into the fence.
Muzarabani is just giving nothing away. Again hits the length hard, on middle and there's extra bounce. Porterfield can only manage to defend it off the back foot.
Length ball, on middle and leg, cramps William Porterfield for room. He manages to keep it out on the leg side.
Muzarabani hits the length hard, on middle. William Porterfield hops to defend.
Length again, around off. Porterfield gets it off the inner half of the bat to mid off.
Length ball, right on the money. Porterfield defends it back to the bowler.
Short of a length, outside off, moving away from the right-hander. Paul Stirling is beaten as he looks to chase it down. End of the Powerplay, Ireland are 34/0.
FOUR! Nicely played! On a length, on middle. Paul Stirling pulls it hard through mid-wicket for a boundary.
A length ball, on off. Paul Stirling punches off the back foot through covers for a couple.
On the pads, this is flicked to mid-wicket.
A length ball, on off. Paul Stirling makes room and cuts it hard towards short backward point who does well to stop it.
On a length, on off. Blocked out.
FOUR! Welcome boundary and a much-needed one! A short ball, outside off. William Porterfield ramps it over the slip cordon and the ball races away to the third man fence.
A length ball, on the hips, flicked to short mid-wicket.
Full and slanting outside off. William Porterfield lets it through.
Short in length, on middle. Paul Stirling pulls it without any control towards deep square leg for a single.
Lovely delivery! Steams a short ball, on middle. Paul Stirling looks to defend inside the line but fails to get any bat on it.
Serves a short ball but it is way outside off. Easy leave for Paul Stirling.
On a length, on off. William Porterfield prods and solidly defends it.
Another bumper, around off. William Porterfield looks to defend but leaves it alone in the end.
Serves a pacy short ball, angling on middle. William Porterfield sits under it.
A length ball, on off. Kept out.
WIDE! Spills it down the leg side. William Porterfield misses his flick. The keeper does well to dive to his right and stop it.
BEATEN! Short in length, outside off. William Porterfield looks to push but gets beaten on the outside edge again.
Hurls a length ball, just around off. William Porterfield looks to play inside the line but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Maiden Over! On a length, outside off. Paul Stirling lets it go.
Length ball outside off. Left alone.
Again serves a short ball, on ff. Paul Stirling stands tall as he looks to defend but gets hit on the gloves and the ball falls way in front of short backward point.
Brilliant delivery! Short in length, outside off. Paul Stirling drops his bat down in time and the ball passes right in front of him to the keeper.
On a length, outside off, it straightens off the deck. Paul Stirling looks to play inside the line but misses.
Short ball, outside off. Paul Stirling leaves it alone.
On middle. Defended back to the bowler.
Short in length, angling in on middle. William Porterfield looks to whip but misses it.
A length ball, outside off. Left alone.
LEG BYE! Angles it onto the pads. Paul Stirling misses his flick and gets hit on the pads. They take a leg bye as the ball rolls on the leg side.
On a length, on middle, this one moves in. Paul Stirling looks to defend but gets an insde edge onto the pads
Full, on off. Paul Stirling drives it nicely but straight to covers.
Length ball, outside off. Porterfield taps it to cover-point.
Back of a length, around leg stump. William Porterfield gets hit high on the bat as he looks to dab it down on the leg side.
Back of a length, on middle. Porterfield hops back and tucks it to mid-wicket.
Short of a good length, angling away from middle. Portefield does well to leave it.
Short and wide, William Porterfield punches it through covers and the ball is racing away. The fielder gives a chase and keeps it down to two runs.
Good-length ball, outside off. Stirling drives it on the up through point for a single.
Shorter in length and outside off. Stirling slashes it down to third man for a run.
Pitched up, on off. Stirling presents a straight bat at it.
Length ball, around off. Stirling stays solid in defense.
A length ball, way outside off. Left alone.
A length ball, on off. Paul Stirling looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
A short ball, on middle. Stirling ducks under it.
A length ball, outside off. kept out.
Length ball, outside off and left alone.
Good-length ball, on middle and angling away. Porterfield leaves it alone.
Back of a length, on off. Stirling gets another inside edge past the stumps for a single to fine leg.
FOUR! STREAKY! Muzarabani hits the length hard, around off. Stirling is late in his cut and gets an inside edge past the stumps and past a diving keeper. The ball races into the fence.
Good-length ball, on off and well left by Paul Stirling.
FOUR! Full and angling down leg. Porterfield clips it off the legs and the ball races into the fine leg boundary. The first one of the innings.
Right on the money from Ngarava. Length and on top of off, Porterfield blocks it out.
Back of a length, on middle. Stirling tucks it behind square on the leg side for a single.
LEG BYE! Length ball, on middle and leg. Porterfield looks to tuck but misses. The ball hits the pad and rolls onto the leg side. They get a leg bye.

Uppish...but SAFE! Fuller ball, on off. Stirling opens the face of the bat and just about gets it over point. The ball is racing away but Luke Jongwe manages to keep it in. William Porterfield calls for the third and gets it. Good running and Stirling is off the mark.
Angling in on the pads and Porterfield flicks it to fine leg for a run.
WIDE! Ngarava starts with a loosener down the leg side. Wided.
Who will bowl from the other end? It is Richard Ngarava.
Back of a length and angling on the pads. Stirling tries to pull awkwardly and the ball pops up after hitting the thigh pad and goes to short square leg. Just one off the first over.
Length again, angling in on leg stump. Stirling misses the tuck and gets hit on the pads. A half-hearted appeal from the visitors.
Length ball, on top of off. Stirling looks to block but gets an inside edge onto the thigh pad.
Porterfield and Ireland are up and running. Length ball, on the pads and keeping a bit low. Porterfield edges it down to third man for a single.
Pitched up again and on off. William Porterfield drives it straight to mid off.
Muzarabani starts with a pitched up delivery, around off. Porterfield plays it to cover.
